note: Small MDC fishing area on the Mississippi floodway near Bird's Point, on a lake scoured out when the levee was blown in the 1927 flood; electric motors only. Camping is in the small paved boat-ramp lot at the lake's north tip, reached by a gravel road along the levee from County Road 301. MDC: 'No amenities are provided. Not recommended as a camping destination.' --Claude
summary: Confirmed the facts (free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit) but MDC itself says 'Camping at Parking Lot - No amenities are provided. Not recommended as a camping destination' - a parking-lot allowance, flagged as a drop candidate. Water is ~10 acres (a lake, not a pond): pond -> lakeview proposed. Pin on the lot is right.
flags: INCLUSION - DROP CANDIDATE: the area page's own Area Information reads '*Camping at Parking Lot - No amenities are provided. Not recommended as a camping destination.' Things to Do still lists 'Individual Campsites' and GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (322) on the paved ramp lot (546, 'Allows_Trailers: No'), but the camping is the boat-ramp parking lot itself (~25x30 m on imagery), which reads as a parking-lot allowance rather than designated sites (the wildlife-agency rule keeps agency-designated sites, not parking-lot allowances). Access is a single gravel road on the levee through the Bird's Point-New Madrid floodway. Recommend drop; AWH to confirm.

WATERFRONT (stored pond) -> lakeview: the water is the 1927 scour lake, ~290 m long and 110-200 m wide on imagery = roughly 10 acres (4 ha), and MDC calls it 'the lake' - above the ~5-acre line, so not a pond. The lot sits at the lake's north tip ~15-25 m from the water, but what lies between is the concrete boat ramp and its apron (a used strip; a ramp is not evidence), so lakefront isn't earned; the open view across the ramp to the lake gives lakeview.
